jessica (support): FYI escalation from ACME. They report inconsistent outputs for the same prompt across calls after the last rollout. Customer claims some requests are routed to a fallback variant and those answers are different. They pasted examples and request IDs.
jessica (support): Sample prompt they sent: 'Summarize the following policy clause and indicate if it requires employee approval: \"All external partnerships require manager signoff if budget > $10k\"'

jessica (support): They invoked our api twice within a minute, got two different verdicts: one said 'No approval required' and the other 'Requires manager approval'. They included request ids: req_06a1 and req_06b3.
jessica (support): Attaching their curl repro (redacted keys):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: acme' \
  -d '{"model":"policy-summarizer", "prompt":"Summarize...", "max_tokens":100}'
```
jessica (support): They suspect routing/fallback to variants after the v2026.03 rollout. Says routing header in logs shows variants: policy-summarizer@v3-q8 and policy-summarizer@v3-q4.
raj (eng-runtime): @jessica thanks. Can you drop the raw request IDs + timestamps? I'll grep router + host logs for those req ids. Also did they observe any 5xx or latency spikes with those calls?
jessica (support): They sent timestamps: 2026-03-12T15:02:11Z (req_06a1) and 2026-03-12T15:02:34Z (req_06b3). No 5xx, both returned 200 but outputs differ. Latency ~220ms for both.
kai (eng-ml): Interesting — q8 vs q4 quantization variants could plausibly change tokenization/outputs, but this magnitude (opposite verdict) seems odd. Do we have eval regressions for these variants on the policy dataset?
taylor (observability): observability-bot attached traces: https://console.redwood.ai/trace/1942001234 (internal) — shows routing decision: 80% -> v3-q8, fallback policy triggered for ~20% to v3-q4 when pool busy. See canary config changed 2h before incident.
raj (eng-runtime): I found the router log lines for those req ids: both hit the same routing rule but different backend chosen due to capacity signals. One went to pool A (v3-q8), the other to pool B (v3-q4). Router logs: \"selected_variant=policy-summarizer@v3-q8\" vs \"selected_variant=policy-summarizer@v3-q4 (fallback)\".
kai (eng-ml): Can you paste the two raw outputs? short redaction ok.
jessica (support): From customer:

req_06a1 -> \"Policy does not require manager approval as written; threshold is ambiguous but appears to be internal budget threshold.\"
req_06b3 -> \"Manager approval required when budget exceeds $10k; advise escalating to manager.\"

jessica (support): Customer says they run batch of 50 identical prompts and ~40% are returning the fallback-style answer.
kai (eng-ml): That ratio is consistent with rollout/canary misconfiguration. Two possibilities: (1) q4 quantization variant has calibration/regression causing different logits for boundary cases; (2) tokenization differences or rounding thresholds cause different final token selection. Need quick repro with deterministic sampling: run with temperature=0 and logprobs to compare.
raj (eng-runtime): I'll force route ACME to v3-q8 for a short window and ask them to rerun. If inconsistency disappears, it's routing. I'll also check our fallback policy thresholds — looks like fallback kicks when pool utilization > 75% and we have permissive fallback mapping to q4. That policy was tweaked in the last deploy.
observability-bot: Trace snapshot created: trace/1942001234/snapshot. CPU heatmap shows burst on pool-B at 15:01Z.
kai (eng-ml): Meanwhile I'll run a diff with deterministic settings. @raj please capture model hashes for both variants and dump per-token logprobs for the two request ids if possible.
raj (eng-runtime): Captured model ids: v3-q8 -> sha256:ab12..., v3-q4 -> sha256:ab12... (same base) but quantization metadata differs. Pulling logs for req_06a1 and req_06b3 now. Will paste masked logprobs.
raj (eng-runtime): Logprobs show divergence starting token 7, top tokens different with small delta. At temperature=0, v3-q8 picks 'No' sequence; v3-q4 picks 'Yes'. The confidence margin is small (~0.8 vs 0.7 normalized). So quantization likely changed boundary behavior.
kai (eng-ml): That matches a quantization calibration issue. Quick mitigation: adjust routing policy to prefer v3-q8 for ACME and set fallback to \"reject and queue\" instead of auto-fallback to q4 for this customer, while we push a recalibrated q4 or disable q4 for policy-summarizer globally.
jessica (support): I'll ask ACME to rerun after forced route. Also offering to pin them to v3-q8 until we resolve. Customer is willing to pin.
raj (eng-runtime): Implemented temporary override: ACME -> policy-summarizer@v3-q8 for 2 hours. Observability shows subsequent calls are consistent. Will open PR to change fallback mapping and add a soft-rate limit before fallback.
kai (eng-ml): I'll start recalibration v3-q4, run evals against policy test set, and prepare a rollback if calibration doesn't fix disagreement rate. Also adding a regression alert when drift between variants > 3% on key prompts.
jessica (support): Thanks team. I'll update the customer: pinning is active, they'll confirm. I'll keep this thread updated with their feedback and any asks for credits/compensation.
raj (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: (1) post mortem of routing tweak; (2) add deterministic logprob capture to request tracing for quick diffs; (3) surface variant agreement metric in console per model.
kai (eng-ml): Agreed. I'll coordinate the calibration and open a changelog entry. 
jessica (support): ACME replied: 'Pin worked, outputs consistent now. Appreciate the quick turnaround.' :thumbsup:
jessica (support): Closing for now but leaving notes for SRE/ML to finish fixes."
